decisions.id: T488-D2 (b): earlier-round edits left standing on that subject
decisions.summary: On any subject where an outside-run dispatch has returned, the whole fresh reset is skipped, so an earlier round's edits stay in edits[s] (what the freeze admits), 'as at HEAD'; Found and left says none.

'As at HEAD' is not a ground for an exception, and the block names the q: page / record-format pairing as THE shape of the wave units' pages, so the carve-out may be the common case, not a corner. The block calls the residual a 'cost' but neither shows it has no wrong outcome nor files it (D15 / FR-009). Fix: reset only the earlier round's edits on that subject while keeping the outside check's (e.g. by what recorded them or when), or state why that separation is impossible; or state, with an observation, that stale edits left in edits[s] change no outcome of the freeze (then Found and left: none stands); or, if they do, fix or file it as a D15 deferral.

decisions.summary: A wave's reading marks (fresh reset, seen, notes read) are applied once for its whole check-wave run at the run's first return, since the pairing is the wave's only hooked launch.
decisions.why: This is the fix the task asks for: a wave's round is counted the way a single dispatch's round is. A single dispatch applies its marks at launch, before any return records edits. Applying them at the run's first return is the nearest equivalent, and it stops a later sibling's reset from wiping a sibling's recorded EDIT blocks, which the freeze would then refuse. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Rows of the run that never paired (no return) still get their seen and notes_read applied.
decisions.why: This is a separate case from D1 and is judged on its own. A single dispatch applies its marks at launch whether or not it returns, and the Workflow launched these rows. Applying them keeps a wave's count the same as a single dispatch's count, which is the task's goal. No wrong outcome results.

decisions.summary: At a run's first return, on a subject where a dispatch outside the run returned unanswered, the fresh reset keeps that dispatch's kept-reply EDIT blocks and drops the rest of the earlier round's edits.
decisions.why: This now completes the reset; it no longer leaves stale edits in place. Keeping the returned check's proposed blocks is the exception that feature 375 FR-003(b) itself makes: the edits the returned checks proposed are applied in one pass. Without it the freeze would refuse correct work. The earlier round's edits are dropped, as the goal requires. Wording note, not blocking: the text says 'a dispatch ... that dispatch's kept reply' in the singular. Where two outside checks have returned unanswered on one subject, FR-003(b)'s plural requires that the blocks of both are kept. The bundle cannot show which the code does.

decisions.summary: The 341 rounded rows' month-old marks are dropped unapplied at the next return, and the 21 never-rounded rows keep theirs, which are inert.
decisions.why: No wrong outcome is left. The block reports that rounds holds none of the 27 units, so no live count moves. Applying a month-old reading now would itself miscount. Leaving inert marks is a difference from tidiness, not a defect (constitution XIV).

decisions.summary: Whether a past ruling read a wrong count is answered by a census of the round-trigger rulings. The first_look side is not replayed from git history.
decisions.why: The question comes from the brief (the coordinating session), not the GM. The census answers it. 14 of the 15 rulings come before any wave row. The 15th is the footnote-flag trip of fixloop::hold, not the round cap. arbiter-owed holds no round trigger. A replay could only matter for a round-cap ruling in range, and there is none, so no defect is left. The new text also correctly drops the earlier false claim that the page text is gone.

decisions.summary: Once a running plan hold is past HOLD_MAX_S, it is purged, and its held text is editable without PLAN_EDIT_OK.
decisions.why: This narrows the plan hold's refusal (feature 385 T85), so it gets a ruling. Tested on a review that is slow but alive past the limit, not on a dead one. Before this change, a hold past HOLD_MAX_S already counted as dead, and PLAN_EDIT_OK passed it. So the only protection removed is the token. A late review's verdict is still checked against the text's digest: make plan-verdict refuses a section that changed while it was reviewed, and per-block digests are recorded. The worst case is therefore a wasted review round, never a verdict landing on changed text. The purpose of the hold, that no verdict approves text it did not read, holds. Keeping the hold would leave a guard refusing correct work on text no live review can approve. It would also load the 3.0 MB state on every Bash call, against the GM's 'prioritize performance improvements' (2026-11-20). The premise that a review returns well inside the limit rests on a GUESS knob's comment, and this ruling does not rely on it. request.md holds nothing of the GM's on the plan hold.
